claims.claim: Amphilochius of Iconium was a fourth‑century Christian bishop of the see of Iconium in Lycaonia (modern Konya, Turkey).
He was born around 339/340, probably at Caesarea in Cappadocia, and died sometime between 394 and 403.

He came from a distinguished Cappadocian family, studied law under the rhetorician Libanius in Antioch, practiced as a lawyer in Constantinople, and was appointed bishop of Iconium about 374, likely at the urging of St Basil.
Amphilochius is known for a small corpus of eight surviving homilies, among them “In natalitia domini,” a sermon on the Nativity of the Lord.
“In natalitia domini” is a festive homily that celebrates the birthday of Jesus Christ and was intended for public reading on the Nativity feast day.
The homily employs the Antiochene typological method of exegesis, rhetorical devices, and orthodox Christology characteristic of fourth‑ and fifth‑century liturgical preaching.

Although Amphilochius wrote polemical works against Arianism, the Macedonians, and ascetic sects, this Nativity homily reflects his pastoral aim of inspiring awe of the incarnation rather than engaging a specific controversy.
